title: Types of Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Chemical Reactions Worksheets: Reaction Types, Activity Series and Products (Chemistry)
standard_text: Construct and revise an explanation for the outcome of a simple chemical reaction based on the outermost electron states of atoms, trends in the periodic table, and knowledge of the patterns of chemical properties.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on types of chemical reactions (NGSS HS-PS1-2): synthesis, decomposition, replacement and combustion, the activity series and predicting products. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Outer electrons and the activity series predict what forms.
body_html:
How to think about it

Reactions follow patterns set by outer electrons.

  • Synthesis A + B → AB; decomposition AB → A + B; single replacement A + BC → AC + B; double replacement AB + CD → AD + CB; combustion: fuel + O2 → CO2 + H2O.
  • A metal replaces another only if it is higher in the activity series.
  • Metal + nonmetal: the charges set the formula of the product.
Example

Zn + CuSO4: reaction?

Zn is above Cu

Answer: yes, Cu forms

Example

Mg + O2: product?

Mg2+ and O2−

Answer: MgO

Common mistakes

  • Thinking any metal can replace any other metal.
  • Forgetting water as a product of combustion.
  • Calling melting or dissolving a chemical change.

faq.q: What are the five main types of reactions?
faq.a: Synthesis, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement and combustion.

faq.q: How does the activity series predict reactions?
faq.a: A metal can replace another metal (or hydrogen in an acid) only if it is higher in the series.

faq.q: What are signs of a chemical reaction?
faq.a: A gas, a precipitate, a color change, light, or a temperature change that comes from new substances forming.

items.q: In a synthesis reaction, what happens?
c: two or more substances combine into one
items.e: A + B → AB.

items.q: A glass bottle is crushed into small pieces. What kind of change is this?
c: a chemical change, because new substances form
a physical change, because the substance stays the same
items.e: No new substance forms.

items.q: What are products?
c: the substances made by a reaction
items.e: Right side.

items.q: Why does sodium react violently with water but gold does not?
c: Sodium loses its 1 valence electron very easily.
items.e: Activity depends on outer electrons.
